title: Microrelease traffic contract and stability schemas (WIP)
content:
Purpose
----
This working doc captures a proposed lightweight "traffic contract" between product feature owners and Platform/Infra/SRE for small, frequent microreleases of LLM-driven features. The aim is to make rapid exposure safe by codifying: (a) explicit telemetry schemas (stability schemas), (b) signal thresholds and actions, (c) synthetic test profiles, and (d) an ops checklist that fits into a 30–90 minute release window.

Context and motivation
----
We repeatedly see: teams want to ship small model/behavior changes quickly, but lack a crisp, machine-readable agreement that says what constitutes "stable" for this microrelease. Current rollouts rely on ad-hoc Slack checks and a few dashboards. This leads to late rollbacks or noisy canaries. A compact traffic contract reduces cognitive load and standardizes responses across cross-functional stakeholders.

Core concepts (short)
----
- Traffic contract: a short (JSON/YAML) artifact attached to the release that lists the main telemetry keys, acceptable deltas, cost guardrails, and rollback actions.
- Stability schema: canonical names and types for telemetry the contract references (latency_p50/p95, error_rate, downstream-accept, generation-quality-score). Teams map their metrics to these canonical keys.
- Exposure modes: tiny-slice (<0.1%), small-batch (0.1–1%), ramp (1–25%). Contract includes allowed modes.

Example traffic contract (human readable)
----
Title: microrelease-qa-reranker-v2
Owner: Search-product (Priya)
Exposure mode: tiny-slice
Slice definition: internal-beta users + 5% of web-traffic sampled by cookie-hash in group B
Duration: 72h initial observation window
Metrics & thresholds:
  - latency_p95: baseline 210ms, max delta +25% -> action: escalate on breach; automatic rollback if sustained >30m
  - error_rate (5xx or model-failure): baseline 0.2%, hard threshold 1.0% -> immediate rollback if >1.0% over 5m
  - rerank-CTR: baseline 0.72, soft threshold -5% relative -> investigation required; maintain exposure if investigation sign-off
  - cost_per_1k_tokens: baseline $0.42, soft threshold +40% -> reduce traffic to 0.1% while investigating
Fallback policy:
  - Serve previous model variant on all users in slice on immediate rollback. If fallback fails, fail open to host default scorer.
Observation hooks:
  - Automated smoke tests every 10m (synthetic queries queue)
  - Sampling of 1 in 100 production requests for debug logs (masked PII)

Stability schema (short spec)
----
Canonical metric keys and expected type/aggregation window:
  - latency_p50 (ms) -> number, rolling 1m and 1h
  - latency_p95 (ms) -> number, rolling 1m and 1h
  - error_rate (pct) -> number, rolling 1m and 15m
  - downstream_accept (pct) -> number, rolling 15m
  - quality_eval_score (0-1) -> number, batch evaluation daily
  - cost_per_1k_tokens (USD) -> number, daily
Teams should add mapping metadata: {my_metric_name: latency_p95}. The console will validate mappings at rollout creation.

Signal orchestration and automated actions
----
- Soft breaches: single-window soft breach triggers a 'notify' to release channel and opens an incident draft with severity S3. Human stakeholders must triage within 30m.
- Hard breaches: sustained hard breach (configurable, e.g., >5m for error_rate) triggers automatic traffic reweight to fallback or full rollback.
- Noise filtering: signals must be evaluated against a minimal sample size (n >= 200) or fall back to smoothed delta over 1h to avoid noisy single-event rollbacks.

Synthetic and stress profiles (for presubmit)
----
We propose three JSON traffic profiles used by the release harness and local sim:
  - baseline-read: 80% read queries, 20% structured prompts, median tokens 32
  - heavy-long: 10% read, 60% long-form generation, median tokens 512, token variance high
  - adversarial-latency: bursty 5s spikes, 200rps sustained for 60s windows to verify autoscaling
Each release must run a 20 minute simulation of the target exposure slice locally or in staging against a captured-production trace before scheduling exposure. The harness exports the canonical metrics so they can be re-used for threshold calibration.

Cross-functional runbook (short flow)
----
1) Release owner attaches traffic contract and stability schema to rollout ticket (JIRA). Console validates mapping.
2) Prestart: staging sim run + smoke. Ops approves and schedules tiny-slice.
3) Start: system routes traffic; automated smoke every 10m; console displays contract badges (OK / SOFT BREACH / HARD BREACH).
4) If SOFT BREACH: oncall + product get Slack ping -> 30m triage window -> apply mitigation (narrow slice, lower weight, pause).
5) If HARD BREACH: automated rollback to fallback; notify pager.
6) Postmortem: export contract telemetry, annotate contract with root cause and recommended contract updates.

Open questions and trade-offs
----
- How prescriptive should contracts be? Minimum viable: 4 signals (latency_p95, error_rate, a quality proxy, cost). Avoid overfitting to 12+ signals for small teams.
- Sampling and privacy: 1-in-100 sample for debug logs might need consent review for EMEA customers. Add opt-out mapping.
- Auto rollback aggressiveness: for high-availability products we want fast rollbacks; for long-running tasks (batch summarization) the thresholds differ. Contract should include product-class.

Short checklist for owners (copyable into JIRA template)
----
- [ ] Create traffic contract YAML and attach to ticket
- [ ] Map team metrics to stability schema keys
- [ ] Run staging sim with 3 profiles and upload canonical metrics snapshot
- [ ] Confirm fallback variant is deployable and smoke-tested
- [ ] Add release channel + escalation list to contract
- [ ] Mark expected observation window and allowed exposure modes

Notes to self / TODOs
----
- Build minimal JSON schema for traffic contract and add to rollout API (Diego).
- Prototype console UI badges that show contract status and last action (Priya).
- Coordinate with legal on sampled debug logs for EMEA (Priya + Legal).
- Decide default sampling min-n for signal gating; propose 200 as starting point.

Appendix: quick sample contract (YAML)
----
---
name: microrelease-qa-reranker-v2
owner: priya@redwood.com
exposure: tiny-slice
slices:
  - name: internal-beta
    selector: user_group == "internal-beta"
metrics:
  latency_p95:
    baseline: 210
    soft_delta_pct: 20
    hard_delta_pct: 30
    aggregation: "1m,1h"
  error_rate:
    baseline_pct: 0.2
    hard_threshold_pct: 1.0
    action: rollback
cost_per_1k_tokens:
    baseline: 0.42
    soft_delta_pct: 40
    action: reduce_exposure
fallback: previous-model-variant
observation_window_h: 72
---

End of working doc. Feedback welcome in comments (add new fields you want in a traffic contract).
